sections.text:
On a beautiful morning, two close friends named Omar and Zaid set off on an exploratory journey through a dense, remote forest.

They were walking together, exchanging conversations and laughing, and they pledged at the beginning of the journey to stand together and support each other, no matter what dangers might arise in this desolate forest.

But, suddenly, while they were walking among the tall trees, they heard a frightening sound.

“Grrrr!”

A very large, predatory brown bear emerged from the bushes and was heading straight towards them, baring its sharp fangs.

Horror gripped the two friends, and the blood froze in their veins from the horror of the sight.

Omar forgot all his promises of friendship and loyalty, and without alerting his friend or helping him, he ran as fast as possible and climbed the nearest tall tree and hid among its thick branches just to save himself.

As for Zaid, he was slower in his reaction, and when he realized the situation, the bear had gotten so close to him that there was no time to run or climb a tree.

Zaid remembered information he read in the past, which said that bears do not eat dead bodies.

He immediately dropped himself to the ground, lay on his back, held his breath completely, and pretended to die with all the skill that the bear might leave him alone.

The huge bear reached Zedd, who was lying on the ground, and began to sniff him cautiously.

The bear brought his wet nose close to Zaid's face, sniffing his ear, nose, and neck, and Zaid held his breath and prayed to God to be saved, as he felt the bear's hot breath on him.

After what seemed like long hours of terror, the bear was convinced that the man was completely dead, so he turned and walked away into the forest, looking for another live prey.

When Omar was sure from the tree that the bear had completely moved away and disappeared from sight, he came down from the tree and ran towards his friend, Zaid, who was slowly getting up and wiping the dirt off his clothes.

Omar said, smiling with a yellow smile to hide his cowardice: “Thank God for your safety, my friend! I saw the bear whispering in your ear for a long time, so what did he say to you?”

Zaid looked at him with a cold look full of disappointment, and said in a firm voice: “The bear whispered golden advice in my ear that I will never forget all my life.”

Omar asked curiously: “What is this advice?”

Zaid replied: “He told me: Beware of traveling or trusting a friend who abandons you at the first appearance of danger and then escapes himself and leaves you to die!”

Omar hung his head in shame after realizing that he had failed the true friendship test, while Zaid continued on his way alone, learning that a true friend is one who shows up in times of trouble, not just times of prosperity.
